- <a id="st-france-saudi-yanbu" class="st-a"></a>**France said on Thursday 24 September it would send troops and air defences to protect Saudi Arabia's Yanbu oil terminal, as Houthi forces fired a fresh barrage of ballistic missiles at the kingdom.** President Emmanuel Macron told French television that Paris planned to "send military assets, meaning soldiers, radars and defence systems to protect" Yanbu — "not to engage in any conflicts but to protect this site." Yanbu is Saudi Arabia's main crude-export terminal on the Red Sea, fed by the East-West pipeline (Petroline — a cross-country line that can carry several million barrels a day, letting oil bypass the Strait of Hormuz). Saudi air defences intercepted Houthi ballistic missiles after warnings were issued for several regions including Mecca, and the Houthis — the Iran-aligned movement that controls much of Yemen — claimed strikes late Thursday on Aramco infrastructure at Yanbu and an unnamed site in Riyadh. The escalation came as fighting inside Yemen intensified, with the group reporting dozens of its own fighters killed in ground clashes. Why it matters: a Western troop deployment to guard Gulf oil infrastructure marks a sharp escalation, and any sustained threat to Yanbu and Petroline feeds directly into oil prices — the same imported-energy channel the Swiss National Bank flagged a day earlier as its main inflation risk.
